oligos.aliases: QFITLIA; fitusiran sodium; ALN-AT3; ALN-AT3SC; SAR439774
oligos.indication: routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in patients aged 12 years and older with hemophilia A or B, with or without factor VIII or IX inhibitors
oligos.developer: Genzyme Corporation / Sanofi (originated at Alnylam Pharmaceuticals)
oligos.max_phase: Approved (US; QFITLIA, DailyMed SPL v6 2025-09-18). Described as investigational in all six journal sources, which predate or straddle approval.
oligos.sequence_locus: NOT_REPORTED - no source in this bundle prints a nucleotide sequence. The US label section 11 DESCRIPTION gives a molecular formula, molecular weight and a structural-formula image only; the image was not read and no sequence was inferred from the formula.
oligos.notes: Single molecule shared by all seven sources; all measurement rows use this local_oligo_key. Chemistry fields come from the US label, section 11 DESCRIPTION: "QFITLIA injection contains fitusiran, an antithrombin-directed double-stranded small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA), which is covalently linked to a ligand containing a triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) moiety." The label's molecular formula contains fluorine and 6 sulfur atoms, which implies 2'-F sugars and phosphorothioate linkages, but NO source states the sugar chemistry or PS count explicitly, so backbone_chemistry, sugar_modifications and ps_count are recorded as NOT_REPORTED rather than inferred. Mechanism (S13 section 12.1): "QFITLIA is a double-stranded siRNA that causes degradation of AT messenger RNA (mRNA) through RNA interference, reducing plasma AT levels." S37 states the targeted AT mRNA sequence is identical in human and mouse, which is why F8-/- mice are a valid pharmacology model, but does not print the sequence.

measurements.control_description: no concurrent control arm; historical comparator is the original 80 mg once-monthly dose regimen (EAIR 2.28 per 100 patient-years)
measurements.effect_vs_control: EAIR 0.82 per 100 patient-years on AT-DR vs 2.28 per 100 patient-years on the original dose regimen

measurements.source_locus: Results, Integrated safety analysis: AEs; and Table 3 (Participants with any thrombotic event, n (%) 4 (1.4); EAIR per 100 patient-years 0.82)
measurements.verbatim_quote: TEAESIs of “any suspected or confirmed thromboembolic events” were reported in 4 (1.4%) participants with AT-DR, corresponding to an EAIR of 0.82 per 100 patient-years ( Table 3 ). None of these events were associated with AT levels of <15% (range, 15.5%-65.3%). Two arterial events (embolic stroke and incidental finding of cerebral infarction) and 2 postoperative venous events (venous thrombosis and DVT) occurred in 1 (0.3%) participant each. Three events were deemed unrelated to fitusiran treatment by the investigator. All 4 participants with thrombotic events had predisposing clinical risk factors; furthermore, doses and frequency of CFC/BPA administered exceeded BMGs in both postoperative venous events ( Table 4 ).
measurements.notes: MIXED ROW. 4 events in 286 participants over 486.0 patient-years. Crucially, none of the four occurred at AT <15% (range 15.5%-65.3%), so residual thrombotic risk on the AT-based regimen is not explained by pharmacodynamic overshoot alone. Three of four were judged unrelated by the investigator; both post-operative venous events involved CFC/BPA dosing above the bleed management guidelines.

measurements.delivery_method: subcutaneous injection
measurements.dose_value: NOT_REPORTED (analysis stratified by achieved AT activity, not by dose)
measurements.n_subjects: NOT_REPORTED (pooled fitusiran clinical programme)
measurements.control_description: the >20% antithrombin activity stratum, in which the incident rate was 0 per 100 patient-years
measurements.effect_vs_control: stratum AT activity <10%: 5.9 vascular thrombotic events per 100 patient-years
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: very low (<10%) AT activity levels were associated with an increased risk of thrombotic events
measurements.source_locus: Methods, Study design and patient population (rationale for the 2020 dosing pause and the AT-based dose regimen)
measurements.verbatim_quote: A thorough evaluation of the thrombotic events was conducted, which showed the incident rate of vascular thrombotic events per 100 patient-years in AT categories <10%, 10% to 20%, and >20% was 5.9, 1.5, and 0, respectively, suggesting that very low (<10%) AT activity levels were associated with an increased risk of thrombotic events.
measurements.notes: THE EXPOSURE-RESPONSE ROW FOR THIS MOLECULE: thrombotic risk is indexed to achieved pharmacodynamic level (antithrombin activity), not to administered dose, with a threshold at AT <10%. The >20% stratum is a genuine measured zero, not missing data. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: S37 (PMC13146349) cites the same 5.9 figure as "an odds ratio for thrombotic risk of 5.9", whereas this source states it as an incident rate per 100 patient-years; this source is the primary report and its wording is used here. No denominator (patient-years per stratum) is given.

measurements.system_model: males aged >=18 y with moderate or severe hemophilia A or B, with or without inhibitors, rolled over from the phase 1 study; phase 1/2 open-label extension LTE14762 (NCT02554773), September 2015 to March 2023
measurements.delivery_method: subcutaneous injection
measurements.dose_value: original dose regimen: 50 mg or 80 mg once monthly
measurements.control_description: NOT_APPLICABLE - individual fatal case
measurements.effect_vs_control: fatal cerebral venous sinus thrombosis in a patient with hemophilia A without inhibitor on the original dose regimen, with concomitant factor concentrate in excess of the bleed management guidelines; last AT activity before the event 15.9%
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The CVST, which was misdiagnosed and treated as a subarachnoid hemorrhage, resulted in death, and the event was recategorized from not related to fitusiran to possibly related to fitusiran.
measurements.source_locus: Table 3 (Summary of thrombotic events), row "Patient with Hemophilia A without inhibitor"; narrative of the same event in Methods (clinical hold) and Table 2 footnotes
measurements.verbatim_quote: Patient with Hemophilia A without inhibitor Original dose regimen Concomitant use of factor concentrate in excess of the current bleed management guidelines 15.9% Hepatitis C positive, cholecystitis, and smoking history (10 cigarettes a day). No history of drug or alcohol abuse. The family history included a fatal ICH in a male sibling with hemophilia at the age of 2 months. CVST occurred in 2017 ∗ The participant was initially suspected of having viral meningitis but was subsequently diagnosed with subarachnoid hemorrhage on the basis of CT imaging. The participant’s clinical course deteriorated despite the administration of FVIII concentrate 2-3 times a day and the participant died secondary to cerebral edema. After this event, the participant’s CT scans were reviewed, and it was confirmed that the initiating event was a CVST, not a subarachnoid hemorrhage. As a result, the assessment of causality was changed from not related to possibility related to fitusiran.
measurements.notes: INDEX FATAL EVENT of the fitusiran programme, initially misdiagnosed as subarachnoid haemorrhage and treated with high-dose FVIII (>30 IU/kg repeatedly), which exceeded the protocol limit. Adjudicated by three independent neuroradiologists. readout_value is the AT activity preceding the event taken from Table 3, not an event count. This is the event referenced as "a fatal event of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis" in the US label (S13).

measurements.system_model: males aged >=18 y with moderate or severe hemophilia A or B, with or without inhibitors, rolled over from the phase 1 study; phase 1/2 open-label extension LTE14762 (NCT02554773), September 2015 to March 2023
measurements.delivery_method: subcutaneous injection
measurements.dose_value: original dose regimen: 50 mg or 80 mg once monthly
measurements.control_description: NOT_APPLICABLE - individual case
measurements.effect_vs_control: right atrial thrombus in a patient with hemophilia B with inhibitor on the original dose regimen with bypassing agent (rFVIIa) in excess of the bleed management guidelines; last AT activity before the event 11.7%
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The TEAEs of atrial thrombosis and transaminases increased were assessed by the investigator as serious and related to fitusiran
measurements.source_locus: Table 3 (Summary of thrombotic events), row "Patient with hemophilia B with inhibitor"; relatedness stated in Results/Safety
measurements.verbatim_quote: Patient with hemophilia B with inhibitor Original dose regimen Concomitant use of BPA (rFVIIa) in excess of the current bleed management guidelines in fitusiran clinical studies 11.7% The participant developed an inhibitor to FIX as an infant with the first few exposures to FIX concentrates. Coincident with the development of the FIX inhibitor the participant manifested with anaphylaxis. He had a prolonged attempt of desensitization to FIX along with immunosuppression, but this culminated in the development of nephrotic syndrome, so this was abandoned. Before the initiation of fitusiran, the participant had almost continuous bleeding into his left elbow and most of the bleeds occurred with the use of an arm sling or splint over weeks at a time despite attempts at intensified dosing and prophylaxis. Atrial thrombosis detected in 2019
measurements.notes: Second of the two thrombotic events in this study, both on the original dose regimen and both with concomitant CFC/BPA above the bleed management guidelines. The mass persisted under FXa-inhibitor anticoagulation, the participant then bled under anticoagulation, fitusiran was resumed and later permanently discontinued after the mass enlarged.

measurements.system_model: males aged >=18 y with moderate or severe hemophilia A or B, with or without inhibitors, rolled over from the phase 1 study; phase 1/2 open-label extension LTE14762 (NCT02554773), September 2015 to March 2023
measurements.delivery_method: subcutaneous injection
measurements.dose_value: original dose regimen: 50 mg or 80 mg once monthly
measurements.timepoint: end point evaluation (last available assessment on the regimen)
measurements.n_subjects: 34 (original dose regimen) / 18 (AT-based dose regimen)
measurements.control_description: pre-fitusiran mean baseline peak thrombin (17 nM (SD, 10))
measurements.effect_vs_control: mean peak thrombin rose from 17 nM (SD, 10) at baseline to 74 nM (SD, 27) at end point on the original dose regimen
measurements.source_locus: Results, Assessment of AT activity levels and TG
measurements.verbatim_quote: Consistent with the mechanism of action of fitusiran, TG increased with AT lowering ( Figure 2 B; supplemental Figure 7 ), from a mean at baseline of 17 nM (SD, 10) to a peak mean of 74 nM (SD, 27) by end point evaluation (ie, last available assessment under the original dose regimen) that remained elevated during the course of fitusiran treatment for the overall participants in the original dose regimen period (ie, 66 months). In the AT-based dose regimen period, TG increased from a mean at baseline of 15 nM (SD, 6) to a peak mean of 88 nM (SD, 29) by end point evaluation (ie, last available assessment on AT-based dose regimen) for the overall participants, although TG assessments were only included for the first 6 months under the AT-based dose regimen.
measurements.notes: ON-TARGET. MAJOR CAVEAT stated by the source: a new batch of thrombin-generation trigger reagent introduced on 06 October 2021 corrupted the assay, so samples from 17 of the 18 AT-based-dose-regimen participants were excluded and only the first 6 months of AT-DR thrombin generation data are included. The 88 nM figure therefore rests on a very small sample. Per-participant trajectories are only in Figure 2B (a spaghetti plot) and were not read.

measurements.n_subjects: NOT_REPORTED
measurements.control_description: on-treatment AT activity before the 2017 clinical hold
measurements.effect_vs_control: mean AT recovered to 69% (SD 17) by 5 months off drug, at a mean recovery rate of 7% per month over 11 months
measurements.source_locus: Results, Assessment of AT activity levels and TG (2017 clinical hold)
measurements.verbatim_quote: During the clinical hold in 2017, AT activity levels in patients previously receiving fitusiran progressively increased. The mean AT recovery was >60% at 5 months after dosing interruption (mean, 69% [SD, 17]), with a mean AT recovery of 7% per month over 11 months. Consequently, TG gradually decreased, with a peak mean of 24 nM (SD, 13) by month 5 of the clinical hold.
measurements.notes: Reversibility of the on-target coagulation defect after stopping the drug; consistent with the US label statement that most patients exceed 60% AT by 6 months.

measurements.effect_vs_control: right middle cerebral artery territory infarct with haemorrhagic transformation and subarachnoid bleed in a 37-year-old male; AT values before the event 9% to 13%; recombinant FVIII given on the 2 days before onset
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The CVA was classified by the investigator as serious and possibly related to fitusiran, resulting in fitusiran discontinuation and study withdrawal.
measurements.source_locus: Results, Safety (AESI narrative for the cerebrovascular accident)
measurements.verbatim_quote: The participant with CVA was a 37-year-old male with a history of right lower extremity deep vein thrombosis not known by the investigator at the time of enrollment (exclusion criterion), and several risk factors including diabetes and possible hypertension and hyperlipidemia around the time of the event. This participant experienced complete left-sided weakness and then likely developed right middle cerebral artery territory infarct hemorrhagic with transformation and subsequent subarachnoid bleed. On 2 consecutive days before the CVA onset, the participant was treated with recombinant FVIII for a spontaneous bleed. The AT values range before the event onset was 9% to 13%. The participant recovered from the event with sequelae 28 days after the onset. The CVA was classified by the investigator as serious and possibly related to fitusiran, resulting in fitusiran discontinuation and study withdrawal.
measurements.notes: readout_value is the pre-event AT activity range, not an event count. AT was in the 9%-13% band, i.e. below the 15% floor later adopted as the safety threshold. Confounders acknowledged by the source: undisclosed prior deep vein thrombosis (an exclusion criterion), diabetes, possible hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and recombinant FVIII on the 2 preceding days.

measurements.effect_vs_control: suspected thrombosis on the papilla of the left eye in a 56-year-old male, onset 87 days after the final fitusiran dose; AT values before onset 9% to 11%; no bleeds and no CFC/BPA use immediately before
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: The thrombosis on papilla was classified as nonserious and assessed by the investigator as possibly related to fitusiran.
measurements.source_locus: Results, Safety (AESI narrative for the thrombosis on papilla)
measurements.verbatim_quote: The participant with thrombosis was a 56-year-old male, with papilledema of both eyes 10 days before the event onset. He experienced pain in eye with the thrombosis onset. No bleeds were reported immediately before the thrombosis, and the participant did not use CFCs or BPAs. It was suspected that there was obstruction in the capillary vessels in the eyes. The investigator considered it possible that the observed papilledema was secondary to a thrombotic event in a capillary that supplies the optic nerve. A brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed inflammatory changes in the maxillary sinus and normal orbital structures; magnetic resonance venography was unremarkable. The AT values range before the thrombosis onset was 9% to 11%. The thrombosis on papilla was classified as nonserious and assessed by the investigator as possibly related to fitusiran.
measurements.notes: Cleanest fitusiran-attributable thrombotic case in this bundle: no concomitant factor concentrate or bypassing agent was used, so the additive-procoagulant confounder present in most other cases is absent. Occurred during follow-up, 87 days after the last dose, while AT was still suppressed.

measurements.control_description: mean baseline AT activity in the same dose group before fitusiran (109.5% (4.4)); normal range approximately 80%-120%
measurements.effect_vs_control: mean nadir AT 18.0%, a reduction of 82.0% (2.2) from baseline
measurements.source_locus: Results, 3.4 Pharmacodynamics
measurements.verbatim_quote: In part D, the mean (standard error of the mean [SEM]) baseline AT activity was 109.5% (4.4) and 100.2% (4.8) in the fitusiran 50 mg and 80 mg dose groups, respectively. Because baseline levels may vary between individuals, we evaluated AT reduction based on percentage of AT activity relative to individual participant baseline. There was consistent reduction in AT activity with fitusiran treatment, evident initially at day 7 and progressing to maximal effect after day 28. The mean nadir AT activity was similar between the two dose groups, specifically, 18.0% in the 50 mg dose group and 12.6% in the 80 mg dose group, corresponding to an 82.0% and 87.4% reduction from baseline, respectively. The minimum residual postdose AT level was 9.8%, observed in the 80 mg dose group.
measurements.notes: ON-TARGET DOSE-RESPONSE ANCHOR: this is the magnitude of antithrombin lowering per dose that makes the later thrombotic events interpretable as overshoot of the same axis. The minimum residual post-dose AT level anywhere in the study was 9.8% (80 mg group), i.e. inside the <10% stratum later linked to the highest thrombotic incident rate.

There were no shifts in PT or aPTT that were reported as clinically significant by the investigators. measurements.notes: ABSENCE ROW (measured null). Routine clotting times and fibrinogen are insensitive to fitusiran pharmacology in vivo, consistent with the in vitro null of S11 (routine assays unaffected by lowering AT to 15%). Individual values are in Figure S3 and were not read. NOTE the hedged wording: "the majority of participants" did not shift, so this is not a claim that every participant was unchanged.

This accumulated into a slightly but significantly 1.4‐fold increased beta‐AT/total AT antigen ratio of 0.28 ± 0.06 for fitusiran‐treated cells compared to 0.20 ± 0.02 for vehicle‐treated cells (P = 0.0199; Figure 6C ).
measurements.notes: ON-TARGET (RNAi knockdown of SERPINC1 in the intended target cell). Beta-antithrombin secretion falls less than total antithrombin; printed as "reduced by 22% ± 15%". Only 29% total knockdown in this short 8 h exposure, far less than the >80% achieved in vivo.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE AND SHAPE. 293 measurement rows for one oligonucleotide (fitusiran) across seven sources. Every row carries a verbatim_quote that was verified programmatically to be an exact character-for-character substring of the named source file after collapsing runs of whitespace to single spaces; whitespace collapsing was necessary because the PMC files are JATS XML flattened to a single line with irregular internal spacing and the DailyMed file is HL7 v3 SPL. XML character entities in the SPL (for example <) were decoded before matching, so quotes such as 'AT activity is <60%' reproduce the document's character content. No quote was paraphrased. 

TIERING. Three tiers are kept deliberately separate and MUST NOT be merged: (1) on-target pharmacodynamics (antithrombin activity, thrombin generation, bleed rates); (2) subclinical hypercoagulability biomarkers (D-dimer, prothrombin fragment 1+2, fibrinogen); (3) clinical thrombotic events. Conflating tier 2 and tier 3 would destroy the distinction the ATLAS programme itself relies on: 44.8% of AT-DR participants had D-dimer elevations >=0.5 mg/L WITHOUT a thrombotic event (S33). 

MIXED FLAGS. Fitusiran is genuinely mixed. Rows where antithrombin lowering or increased thrombin generation is the intended effect carry on_target_effect=true. Rows where the same axis overshoots (thrombotic events, AT <15%, D-dimer/PF1+2 elevation, additive peak thrombin with CFC/BPA) carry BOTH on_target_effect=true and unintended_toxicity=true. Bleeding events in these hemophilia populations are residual disease, not drug toxicity, and carry neither flag. 

CONTRADICTION 1 (IMPORTANT). S34 states the figure 5.9 as an 'incident rate of vascular thrombotic events per 100 patient-years' in the AT <10% stratum. S37 cites the same value from the same underlying analysis as 'an odds ratio for thrombotic risk of 5.9'. These are different statistical quantities. S34 is the primary clinical report and its wording was used for the extracted row; anyone modelling exposure-response should treat the units of 5.9 as uncertain until the primary analysis (S34 reference 29) is checked. 

CONTRADICTION 2. Prothrombin fragment 1+2 incidence: S13 (US label Table 3) prints '7' in a column headed 'Number of Patients (%) N=286'; S33 reports 17 of 286 (5.9%) for the same integrated AT-DR population. The label value is read as a percentage because the table is restricted to reactions occurring in >=5% of patients and the smallest cell is 5 (5 patients of 286 would be 1.7%). The two figures still disagree (7% vs 5.9%), most likely because of different pooled data cuts. Both rows are retained with the discrepancy noted. 

CONTRADICTION 3. S34 reports, for the same regimen and period, both a 'mean reduction of 96% (SD, 12)' and a 'mean AT percentage change from baseline of -86% (SD, 4)'. These cannot both describe the same quantity. Both numbers are recorded as printed and the discrepancy is flagged on the affected rows. 

SOURCE DEFECT IN S11 TABLE 1. In the aPTT block 'Dade Actin FSL (ellagic acid) on BCS XP System', FIX series, target FIX level 20%: the printed means are 20.4 (0.7) at 15% AT and 30.2 (0.4) at 100% AT, which is about a -32% change, yet the printed '% change' for that cell is 0.6. One of the printed numbers is almost certainly a typographical error. Values are recorded exactly as printed and the row is flagged; do NOT recompute a percentage change from these two cells. A second, smaller defect: in S11 Table 2 the FIX chromogenic row's fourth column header is printed as '100/15' where the pattern requires '100/1000'. 

S11 IS NOT A DRUG-EXPOSURE STUDY. In S11 the low-antithrombin state was produced by diluting control plasma with AT-immunodepleted plasma, and fitusiran was added directly to plasma in vitro at ~1000 ng/mL. No RNA interference can occur in that system. All S11 rows therefore carry on_target_effect=false: they are an analytical-interference control, not pharmacology. Their value to this dataset is exactly that - they are the null rows that stop an assay artefact being scored as toxicity, showing that neither lowering AT to 15% nor 10x-therapeutic fitusiran in the tube perturbs routine PT, aPTT, TT, one-stage, chromogenic or Nijmegen-Bethesda assays. 

NO FIGURE VALUES WERE READ. Where a quantity exists only in a plotted panel (S35 supplemental Figure 3 for D-dimer/PF1+2/fibrinogen trends; S36 Figures 1B, 2, S2-S4; S34 Figures 1-3 spaghetti/box plots; S37 Figures 5A and 5B) the row carries readout_value NOT_REPORTED with readout_is_qualitative true and says so in notes. The single exception is S37's Figure 5A, for which the Discussion prints a numeric summary ('increased by about 20%'), transcribed as 20 with the hedge recorded. 

ASSAY CAVEAT IN S34. A new batch of thrombin-generation trigger reagent introduced on 06 October 2021 corrupted the assay; samples from 17 of the 18 AT-based-dose-regimen participants were excluded and only the first 6 months of AT-DR thrombin generation are analysable. The AT-DR peak thrombin of 88 nM therefore rests on a very small sample. 

DENOMINATOR HAZARD. The same programme is reported with several overlapping denominators: 286 (AT-DR integrated safety), 270 (fixed-dose/ODR integrated safety), 335 (pooled fixed + AT-DR), 227 (ATLAS-OLE enrolled), 213 (ATLAS-OLE on AT-DR), 67/65 (ATLAS-PPX), 34/18 (phase 1/2 OLE), 17 (phase 1 part D). Rows from different sources describing 'the fitusiran programme' overlap in patients and MUST NOT be summed. 

SELECTION BIAS ON THE THROMBOTIC RATES. Participants with established thrombophilia, prior arterial or venous thromboembolism, significant valvular disease, atrial fibrillation, AT activity <60% at screening or platelet count <=100,000/uL were excluded from these studies (stated in S13 section 14 and S33). The 1.4% / 0.82 per 100 patient-years AT-DR thrombotic rate is therefore a rate in a thrombosis-selected-out population. 

PLATELETS. Exactly one platelet-adjacent row was extracted (S36, platelet_coag_crosstalk), and only because the source ties platelet count to fibrinogen and PT/INR as a composite check for pathological clot formation accompanying D-dimer elevation. It carries no platelet count and is not a thrombocytopenia row. Platelet counts reported elsewhere in these sources (for example the <=100,000/uL enrolment exclusion) were left out as belonging to the separate thrombocytopenia endpoint. 

REGIMEN TAGGING. dose_value distinguishes the abandoned fixed 80 mg once-monthly original dose regimen (ODR) from the approved antithrombin-based dose regimen (AT-DR, 50 mg every 2 months titrated to AT 15-35%). This matters: thrombotic risk is regimen-dependent (2.6%/2.3 per 100 person-years on ODR vs 1.4%/0.8 on AT-DR), so ODR and AT-DR rows must never be pooled. 

VALUE-TO-QUOTE TRACEABILITY. For 288 of the 293 rows the readout_value appears literally inside that row's own verbatim_quote. The five exceptions are declared here: four zero-event rows (S33 fatal TEAEs, S34 thrombotic events on the AT-based regimen, S36 thrombotic events, S37 thrombotic events) where readout_value 0 encodes a null the source states in words rather than as a printed digit; and the S13 prothrombin fragment 1.2 row, where HL7 SPL table markup makes the row label and its numeric cell non-contiguous so the quote is the row label and the value 7 is the adjacent cell of the same row of Table 3. Each of the five says so in its own notes field. 

MODIFICATIONS ARRAY IS EMPTY BY DESIGN. No source in this bundle publishes a fitusiran nucleotide sequence or any per-position chemistry legend, so no per-position rows could be written without fabrication.
refused_rows:
1. FITUSIRAN SEQUENCE AND PER-POSITION CHEMISTRY. Not extracted. The US label gives a molecular formula containing F and S6 and a structural-formula image, which would allow a plausible guess at 2'-F sugars and 6 phosphorothioate linkages, and the fitusiran sequence is publicly known from other literature. Neither was written: no source IN THIS BUNDLE prints a sequence or a per-position legend, and the rule is that missing means NOT_REPORTED. The structural-formula image was not read. 
2. ALL FIGURE-ONLY NUMERIC VALUES. Individual antithrombin and peak-thrombin trajectories (S34 Figures 2A/2B), D-dimer time courses (S36 Figures S3/S4), the D-dimer / prothrombin fragment 1+2 / fibrinogen curves for fitusiran vs prior prophylaxis (S35 supplemental Figure 3), the thrombin-generation-versus-AT-quartile box plots (S36 Figure 2), and the diluted-PT and thrombin-generation bars for the alpha/beta-AT titration (S37 Figures 5A/5B) all contain numbers that would be useful and are all refused. Qualitative rows with readout_value NOT_REPORTED were written instead where the text states a direction. 
3. NON-OLIGONUCLEOTIDE COMPARATOR COHORTS IN S37. Congenital type 1 antithrombin deficiency (2 patients: AT activity 40.1% and 42.7%, beta/total ratios 0.22 and 0.14) and liver cirrhosis by Child-Pugh class (total AT antigen 172 / 108 / 81 ug/mL for A/B/C, beta/total ratio 0.07 to 0.12). These are quantitative coagulation data but no oligonucleotide was administered, so attaching them to local_oligo_key FITUSIRAN would misattribute them. They are mechanistically important context (the isoform shift is a general consequence of low AT synthesis, not a fitusiran-specific effect) and are recorded here rather than as rows. 
4. NON-COAGULATION TOXICITY. Hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST >3x ULN in 32% and 18% on 80 mg monthly; 3.4-3.5% on AT-DR; one moderate hepatic injury case), gallbladder disease (17% and 4% cholecystectomy on fixed dosing vs 3.8% and 0.3% on AT-DR), injection site reactions, anti-drug antibodies, and the rat/Tg-rasH2 mouse carcinogenicity and fertility studies are all present in these sources and all refused: they belong to other endpoints. Hepatotoxicity is noted here only because it co-occurs with the coagulation findings in the same participants. 
5. HAEM-A-QOL AND OTHER PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES. Numerous and well reported, but not a coagulation readout. 
6. PHARMACOKINETIC PARAMETERS (Cmax, AUC, t1/2, Vss/F, CL/F, urinary recovery, protein binding). Refused as not coagulation readouts, although S13 section 12.3 tabulates them fully and they would be needed for any PK/PD model. 
7. AGGREGATE 'ANY TEAE' / 'ANY TESAE' COUNTS. Refused where the composite mixes coagulation and non-coagulation events and cannot be resolved to a coagulation readout. The single exception is the 'no fatal TEAEs with AT-DR' absence row from S33, retained because it bounds fatal thrombotic outcomes on that regimen; its all-cause scope is stated in its notes. 
8. THE PER-EVENT DETAIL OF S13's TABLE 3 ADVERSE-REACTION COLUMN beyond prothrombin fragment 1.2. The column header 'Number of Patients (%)' is genuinely ambiguous and only the prothrombin fragment row is a coagulation readout, so no other row of that table was extracted. 
9. CROSS-SOURCE ARITHMETIC. No row was created by computing a rate, a percentage change, a confidence interval or a pooled denominator from numbers the sources did not print together. Where a percentage change is quoted in effect_vs_control it is the source's own printed value.
